headline: Task Management covers 15 tickets all marked ready for release; the code review confirmed 6 of them — the background scheduler, task dependencies, the Kanban board, Excel bulk import, the calendar view and the AI task planner — while the remaining 9 could not be settled from the files the analysis examined.
what_is_there: There is a working background scheduler that wakes on a timer and runs due tasks on separate threads, task-to-task dependencies where a task waits for all its prerequisites, a drag-and-drop Kanban board with add/edit/context menus, a calendar view of scheduled tasks, Excel-based bulk task import, and an AI planner that turns a plain-English description into scheduled tasks.
what_is_unclear: Nine items — the underlying task record and its statuses/priorities, recurring and cron scheduling, holiday and working-day rules, task chaining modes, input/output modes and artifact storage, the execution worker with per-task model and skill selection, the approval gate, Teams/Outlook/in-app notifications, and the task editor form — were not confirmed, mostly because the files pulled for review turned out to be unrelated or none were retrieved at all; this says nothing about whether they exist. Two confirmed items also had a detail left open: the three-concurrent-task limit and dependency cycle detection were not visible in the portions read.
suggested_action: Ask the team to point to the specific code for the nine unconfirmed items — particularly the task record/status model, recurrence and holiday scheduling, and notifications — so a second pass can look in the right place.
